Define controlled imputation strategies for count outcomes

Source: R/impute_count.R
count_strategy.Rd

count_strategy() defines how the model-based mean for a missing count is obtained and optionally adjusted during imputation. The base strategy is applied first. A rate_multiplier then multiplies its model-based mean, or fixed_rate replaces that mean by a fixed event rate.

Usage 

count_strategy(
  base = c("MAR", "JR", "CR"),
  rate_multiplier = 1,
  fixed_rate = NULL,
  fixed_rate_scale = c("rate", "lambda"),
  period = NULL
)

get_count_strategies(...)

Arguments

base

Character. The base count imputation strategy, one of "MAR", "JR", or "CR".

rate_multiplier

A non-negative numeric scalar multiplying the model-based mean for affected missing cells.

fixed_rate

NULL or a non-negative numeric scalar. When set, it replaces the model-based rate of affected missing cells. Its meaning depends on fixed_rate_scale; see the section on fixed rates.

fixed_rate_scale

The scale of fixed_rate: "rate" (default), an event rate per unit of duration, or "lambda", the negative-multinomial lambda scale. Must only be specified together with fixed_rate.

period

NULL or a vector of period values. If supplied, the rate adjustment is restricted to missing cells in these periods. The base strategy still applies to other missing periods.

...

Named count_strategy objects to add to the built-in strategies.

Value

count_strategy() returns a count_strategy object. get_count_strategies() returns a named list of these objects for use in the strategies argument of impute().

Details

get_count_strategies() returns the built-in MAR, JR and CR count strategies together with any named user-defined strategies supplied through .... For count outcomes, the strategy is assigned at the subject level and applies to every missing positive-duration period for that subject. No ICE time is supplied or inferred; consequently, JR and CR are not restricted to periods after an ICE.

Fixed rates and SAS compatibility

With the default fixed_rate_scale = "rate", fixed_rate is a marginal event rate per unit of the duration variable: a missing cell with exposure L has unconditional mean L * fixed_rate, the same for every posterior draw, treatment arm and base strategy.

fixed_rate_scale = "lambda" reproduces the fixed-rate option of the SAS macro NM_Rand13.sas (Roger, 2021), which fixes the rate on the negative-multinomial lambda scale. The unconditional mean is then L * fixed_rate / phi, where phi is the dispersion parameter of the current posterior draw (from the subject's arm for MAR, and from the mapped reference arm for JR and CR). The implied event rate therefore changes from draw to draw and between arms, and becomes arbitrarily large as phi approaches zero (nearly Poisson data). impute() warns when the SAS lambda implies a rate more than 100 times the model-based rate of the same cell in any posterior draw. Use this scale only to reproduce SAS results.

For both scales, the imputed count is drawn conditionally on the subject's observed cells. Its conditional mean is the unconditional mean multiplied by (1 / phi + y_obs) / (1 / phi + mu_obs), where y_obs and mu_obs are the subject's observed total count and its model-based mean.

References

Roger JH (2021). NegMult20210313: SAS macros for imputation of recurrent event data for partially observed off-treatment data. DIA Missing Data Working Group.

Examples 

fixed_rate <- count_strategy(
    base = "MAR",
    fixed_rate = 0.003,
    period = "3"
)
fixed_lambda <- count_strategy(
    base = "MAR",
    fixed_rate = 0.0021,
    fixed_rate_scale = "lambda",
    period = "3"
)
double_rate <- count_strategy(
    base = "MAR",
    rate_multiplier = 2,
    period = "3"
)
get_count_strategies(
    FIXED_RATE = fixed_rate,
    FIXED_LAMBDA = fixed_lambda,
    DOUBLE_RATE = double_rate
)
